title: The Lost Sheep
review_status: DRAFT: retelling and wondering questions require theological and editorial review before release.

source.note: Original child-friendly retelling written for this prototype; not a quotation of any translation. See also Matthew 18:12-14.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: This is a story Jesus told. Let's carry the material to the table, and listen.

segments.text: Jesus told a story about a shepherd. The shepherd had one hundred sheep, and he knew every one of them.
One day, one little sheep wandered away, far from the others, until it was lost.
The shepherd counted his sheep: ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine... One was missing!
So he left the ninety-nine together, and he went out into the wilderness to look for the one that was lost. He searched and searched until he found it.
When he found it, he was so happy! He lifted the sheep onto his shoulders and carried it all the way home.
He called his friends and neighbors together and said, "Be happy with me! I have found my sheep that was lost!"
And Jesus said that there is joy like this in heaven over one who is found.

wonderings: I wonder how the lost sheep felt, far away all by itself.
I wonder how the shepherd knew that one was missing.
I wonder how the sheep felt, carried home on the shepherd's shoulders.
I wonder who the shepherd might be.

steps.prompt: When you're ready, return each figure to its place in the box.

feedback.mismatch: That place is shaped for a different figure.
feedback.all_good: Each figure is resting in its place.

outro.speaker: narrator
outro.text: The material is back on the shelf. It will be here whenever you want to return to it.

journal_line: I listened to the story of the shepherd who went looking for the one lost sheep, and carried it home.
